explanation:
[EFFECT] Humidity has a non-monotonic shape with a sharp early jump. At extremely low humidity (below ~5%) demand is strongly suppressed (~–1.0). Contribution jumps quickly to a slight positive plateau (~+0.10) at moderate humidity and stays roughly flat up to about 60%, then gradually declines, reaching about –0.3 at 100% humidity.
[IMPORTANCE] Fifth in importance (0.083), close to month; the extreme low-humidity penalty is notable but affects relatively few hours.
[RECOMMENDATION] Hour of day and temperature are by far the two strongest drivers of predicted demand, so operational planning — such as bike redistribution and staffing — should be tightly organised around the two daily rush-hour peaks (around 8 a.m. and 5–6 p.m.) and scaled up noticeably in mild to warm weather while scaling back during cold spells or the early hours of the morning.
